## `new` and `returnOriginal` options deprecated

As of Mongoose 9.2.0 ([#16008](https://github.com/Automattic/mongoose/pull/16008)), the `new` and `returnOriginal` options for `findOneAndUpdate()` and `findOneAndReplace()` are deprecated in favor of `returnDocument`. Passing either option still works, but now prints a runtime deprecation warning:

```txt
[MONGOOSE] Warning: mongoose: the `new` option for `findOneAndUpdate()` and `findOneAndReplace()` is deprecated. Use `returnDocument: 'after'` instead.
```

Update your queries as follows:

* Use `returnDocument: 'after'` instead of `new: true` or `returnOriginal: false`
* Use `returnDocument: 'before'` instead of `new: false` or `returnOriginal: true`

```javascript
// Before
const doc = await Model.findOneAndUpdate(filter, update, { new: true });

// After
const doc = await Model.findOneAndUpdate(filter, update, { returnDocument: 'after' });
```

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).

a.quote: * Use `returnDocument: 'before'` instead of `new: false` or `returnOriginal: true`
